Use the exact same SciPy test file from the buggy/fixed revisions to ensure identical tolerance settings.

The strategy assumes the bug is exercised in SciPy.stats._morestats.boxcox_llf for lmb near 0 and that the regression test is present in the test file for both revisions. Ensure you run on the revisions where the test is added (or apply the test patch to both revisions before running).

oracle.reference_source: Project regression test in scipy/stats/tests/test_morestats.py (assert_allclose(llf, -15.32401272869016598)); expected value comment says it was computed with mpsci/mpmath.mp.dps=100.
oracle.why: The test asserts the computed llf matches a specific scalar oracle value; the success/failure of the assert_allclose determines the transition.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy revision 673a15da1366, test_instability_gh20021 fails because boxcox_llf computes the log-variance term using an unstable intermediate near lambda=0 (per PR description: logx = lmb*logdata - log(abs(lmb)); logvar = _log_var(logx) without factoring the division by lmb), yielding llf that is not within assert_allclose tolerance of -15.32401272869016598.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision that implements the stable computation around lambda=0 (logx = lmb*logdata; logvar = _log_var(logx) - 2*np.log(abs(lmb))), test_instability_gh20021 passes with llf matching -15.32401272869016598 within assert_allclose tolerance.
